Kimberly-Clark won EU conditional approval for its $40B purchase of Kenvue, removing a major hurdle and narrowing the deal-completion risk discount.

Houthi ballistic missiles hitting Riyadh and Iran fortifying nuclear sites keep missile-defense and counter-drone demand rising; L3Harris just delivered its first VAMPIRE counter-drone systems to the US Army.

European expansion via the cellumation acquisition broadens Symbotic's warehouse-automation reach.

top_buys.pitch: Large-cap refiner leverage to widening crack spreads from a heavy-oil freight squeeze and Middle East supply fear.
top_buys.why: Small refiners like PBF, PARR and CVI jumped 6-14% as Americas heavy crude gluts while Asia and Europe scramble for barrels — that spread is exactly what refining margins feed on. Phillips 66 has big refining plus midstream and marketing, and large caps usually follow the small-cap move with a lag. Energy was the best sector last week (+4.9%), so the tide is with the trade.
top_buys.risks: A US-Russia diesel deal flooding product markets, or a fast Middle East de-escalation, would compress cracks quickly.
top_buys.watch: Weekly EIA product inventories and any concrete news on the US-Russia diesel arrangement.

top_buys.pitch: EU conditional clearance removes the biggest hurdle to Kimberly-Clark's $40B takeover.
top_buys.why: Antitrust approval in Europe is a major de-risking step for a cross-border consumer deal of this size, and merger spreads typically narrow steadily rather than all at once. Consumer staples was the second-strongest sector last week, so the tape supports it. My M&A calls have been my most reliable category.
top_buys.risks: Remaining regulatory jurisdictions could impose conditions, and a deal re-cut or walk-away would hit the shares hard.
top_buys.watch: Shareholder vote timing and remaining regulatory approvals.

top_buys.pitch: Counter-drone and missile-defense demand grows with every Houthi missile fired at Riyadh.
top_buys.why: Saudi Arabia is striking Yemen while Houthis keep launching ballistic missiles at Riyadh airports, and Iran is reportedly fortifying nuclear sites ahead of possible US strikes. L3Harris just delivered its first VAMPIRE counter-drone systems to the US Army, directly in the product category this conflict is consuming. Defense budgets respond to sustained conflict with multi-quarter order flow, which the market often underprices day to day.
top_buys.risks: A ceasefire or peace deal would deflate defense sentiment, and industrials were the second-weakest sector last week.
top_buys.watch: New counter-UAS and interceptor contract awards and L3Harris's next quarterly report.

top_buys.pitch: Approval to prepare for domestic business in China opens the world's biggest payments market.
top_buys.why: After years of blocked access, Visa getting the green light to prepare domestic operations in China is a structural long-term positive. These regulatory milestones tend to be under-reacted to on day one because revenue is years away, but they lift the long-run growth story. Financials have been one of the stronger sectors recently.
top_buys.risks: Implementation could take years, local competition is entrenched, and US-China tensions could reverse the approval.
top_buys.watch: Any formal licensing timeline from Chinese regulators and Visa's next earnings commentary on China.

top_buys.pitch: European expansion via the cellumation acquisition broadens Symbotic's warehouse-automation reach.
top_buys.why: Symbotic is buying German materials-handling firm cellumation, giving it a European foothold beyond its US-heavy, Walmart-concentrated base. Diversifying customers and geography addresses the main bear argument on the stock. Automation demand remains a funded capex priority even as chip stocks wobble.
top_buys.risks: High-multiple, volatile stock with customer concentration; integration of a European acquisition can be slow and dilutive.
top_buys.watch: Next quarterly backlog update and any new non-Walmart customer announcements.
